title: Runtime adapter routing charter and ownership map
content:
Purpose and intent:
This note sketches an operational charter for runtime adapters and the routing policies that bind them to the control plane. The goal is to make ownership explicit (who writes, who reviews, who runs), to define a small canonical surface for adapters, and to set concrete SLO and failure-mode expectations for multi-region routing and fallback.

Audience:
Platform engineers, runtime/serving teams, edge/gateway engineers, SRE, and anyone touching orchestration routing rules and adapter contracts.

Problem statement (short):
As we scale Dedicated and Private deployments across regions, ambiguous ownership of routing logic and adapter behavior has led to inconsistent fallbacks, high-latency hot paths, and repeated rollbacks. This charter aims to reduce blast radius by:
- Narrowing the adapter surface to a minimal RPC/HTTP contract.
- Prescribing routing policy primitives for latency/cost/region decisions.
- Mapping clear team ownership for each functional boundary.

Core definitions (for this doc):
- Adapter: runtime-side component responsible for translating orchestration calls into model runtime actions (load model shards, manage KV cache, run inference, report metrics).
- Orchestrator: control plane service that makes placement and routing decisions (region, node pool, model variant).
- Gateway: API layer that accepts external requests and applies coarse policy (auth, tenant routing, rate limit) before hitting orchestrator.
- Routing policy: declarative set of rules expressing preferred region, max-latency budget, fallback chain, and allowed model variants per tenant/tier.

Proposed adapter contract (minimal):
- Health check endpoint: /healthz returning {status, modelVersionsLoaded, kvCacheStatus, lastReloadTs}.
- Inference API: POST /v1/infer with headers: X-Tenant, X-Request-Id, X-Trace. Body: {model, prompt, options}. Response MUST include per-token timing (server-side) and maxSequenceLength.
- Control hooks: POST /v1/control/reload, POST /v1/control/evict-kv, GET /v1/control/stats. All authenticated with mTLS; token-based fallback is disallowed for these endpoints.
- Telemetry: adapters emit standardized metrics: adapter_latency_ms, kv_hit_ratio, memory_resident_bytes, active_sessions. Tags: region, pool, tenant, model_variant.

Routing policy DSL (sketch):
A compact policy structure the orchestrator understands:
- priority: latency|cost|isolation
- preferred_regions: [region-code list]
- max_tail_latency_ms: integer
- fallback_chain: [compatible_variant_1, variant_2, hosted_fallback]
- cache_policy: prefix|none|shared
- routing_constraints: {requires_gpu:true/false, quantized:true/false}
Note: this is intentionally small to keep routing decisions fast in the orchestrator.

Ownership map (high level):
- API Gateway: team = eng-gateway. Responsibilities: auth, tenant sharding, coarse rate limiting, request validation, edge-level canary flags. Owns first-line SLA to customers (5xx handling, 99.9% availability target for hosted API).
- Orchestrator: team = eng-platform-engineering (orchestration subset). Responsibilities: routing policy evaluation, candidate selection, region failover sequencing, model variant resolution, writing routing decisions to a persistent decision log. Owns orchestration SLO for decision latency (p95 < 8ms).
- Adapter runtime: team = eng-serving-runtime. Responsibilities: implem of adapter contract, local batching, KV cache, model lifecycle. Owns runtime SLOs (inference p50/p95/p99 targets per model class).
- Observability/Telemetry ingestion: team = eng-observability. Responsibilities: schema for adapter metrics/traces and retention policies.

Concrete ownership table (textual):
- Edge auth + tenant mapping -> eng-gateway
- Routing policy definition (DSL, validation) -> eng-platform-engineering (policy authors), reviewed by eng-serving-runtime for compatibility
- Model variant registry and compatibility matrix -> eng-serving-runtime (owner), product/ML to validate quality constraints
- Decision log storage & audit -> eng-platform-engineering + eng-infra for ops
(We will keep the single source of truth in the decision-log service with write-only API from orchestrator.)

SLOs and budgets (suggested):
- Orchestrator decision latency: p50 < 3ms, p95 < 8ms, p99 < 50ms
- Gateway extra latency budget: p50 < 4ms, p95 < 10ms (routing + auth)
- Adapter cold-start for new model load: < 12s for a model shard (tracked as background work)
- Inference tail latency: dependent on model class, but adapter must expose p50/p95/p99 labels and not hide internal retries.

Multi-region fallback flow (example):
1) Gateway receives request for tenant T in region eu-west1, calls orchestrator with routing hint and desired policy (latency|cost).
2) Orchestrator evaluates policy and checks decision-log cache; picks primary candidate in eu-west1 pool A.
3) Orchestrator returns candidate; gateway proxies to adapter endpoint in eu-west1.
4) On adapter failure or SLA breach (e.g., 503 or > max_tail_latency), gateway should call orchestrator with failure event and receive next candidate from fallback_chain.
5) Orchestrator increments adaptive penalty for the failed adapter/pool and adjusts future selection weights.

Failure modes and safe defaults:
- Unknown model variant: orchestrator rejects early with 400 and includes suggested compatibleVariants.
- Adapter telemetry missing: treat as degraded, deprioritize for routing.
- Region partition: if control-plane cannot reach a region for 30s, mark region as unelectable for routing decisions but continue serving cached decisions for short window (TTL 1m).

Change control and rollout playbook (short):
- Any change to adapter contract requires: adapter-side PR (unit tests), orchestrator policy validator changes, integration test against a contract conformance harness, and opt-in canary rollout (eng-gateway route flag + telemetry guardrails).
- Emergency rollback: orchestrator supports per-tenant policy override to force modelVariant or region. SRE runbook: set override -> flush cache -> monitor 5m.

Onboarding checklist for new adapter teams:
- Implement /healthz and control hooks with mTLS.
- Expose metrics with agreed schema and tag set.
- Add unit tests for contract conformance and publish to the conformance repo.
- Open PR to add variant compatibility metadata to the model registry.
- Run canary with a single internal tenant for 48h and confirm telemetry.

Open questions and work items (short list):
- Q: How aggressive should the orchestrator be about penalizing variants for transient latency spikes? (ticket: PLATFORM-1342)
- Q: Where to host the decision-log so cross-region reads are low-latency but still auditable? (follow-up: evaluate Cockroach vs Dynamo-style regional replication)
- WIP: policy DSL serialization format (JSON v.s. protobuf) and validation library to be decided by 2025-01-31.

Next steps (practical):
1) Post this doc to Confluence as the draft charter and solicit review from eng-serving-runtime and eng-gateway.
2) Spin up a small conformance harness issue (PLATFORM-1429) to codify the minimal adapter contract.
3) Start a canary of the new decision-log TTL behavior in eu-west1 for 2 weeks.

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus feedback on the adapter contract and the routing DSL primitives. Keep the DSL minimal; we will iterate with concrete experiments.
- If your team wants ownership, call it out and provide the single lead and an oncall contact.

Appendix: quick links and debug commands (examples)
- Query decision log: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://decision-log.redwood.internal/v1/decisions?tenant=T
- Adapter health check example: curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://adapter.eu-west1.internal/healthz
- Telemetry dashboard: link to Grafana panel: /d/adapter-health/adapter-latency

End of draft.
